content.title: About
content.content: Cheese fondue is a classic Swiss dish consisting of melted cheese into which pieces of bread, vegetables or meat are dipped. The traditional blend uses Gruyère and Emmental, with white wine, garlic and spices. It is served hot in a communal pot.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fondue originated in the Alpine regions in the 19th century as a way to use leftover cheese.
The traditional serving vessel is a wooden pot kept warm by a small candle.
Switzerland celebrates National Fondue Day on March 11.
There are many variations: meat fondue (Bourguignonne), chocolate fondue, and vegetarian versions.
The original recipe calls for dry white wine, which gives the dish its distinctive aroma.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: The cheeses used in fondue provide a high amount of calcium, essential for bones and teeth.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Melted cheese supplies high‑quality protein that supports muscle maintenance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cheeses contain vitamin B12 and riboflavin, which help the nervous system function.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: Fermented cheeses may contribute beneficial bacteria to the gut microbiome.

items.title: Phosphorus content
items.content: Phosphorus in cheese aids cellular energy metabolism.

items.title: High in fat and calories
items.content: Fondue is rich in saturated fats, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People who cannot digest lactose may experience discomfort.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Cheeses are often salty; those with hypertension should limit intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve fondue in a warmed pot and dip bite‑size pieces of baguette, boiled potatoes, pickled vegetables or cooked meat. A splash of wine or a dab of mustard can enhance flavor. Prepare small batches to keep the cheese smooth.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool leftover fondue, transfer it to an airtight container, and refrigerate for up to 2 days. Reheat gently over low heat while stirring to prevent curdling.
